findings.justification: Real bug: refFor returns the version verbatim including Go's `+incompatible` suffix, which the GitHub compare API does not recognize as a tag, so a legitimate common v2+ bump is reported resolved:false and silently denied upstream context. Concrete fix (strip the suffix).
findings.body: Bug: `refFor` returns the version string verbatim for non-pseudo-versions, including Go's `+incompatible` suffix (e.g., `v2.0.0+incompatible`). The GitHub compare API doesn't recognize `v2.0.0+incompatible` as a tag ref — the actual git tag is `v2.0.0` without the suffix. This causes `compareCommits` in `fetchUpstreamChangeSummary` to fail and the bump to be reported as `resolved: false`, even though the upstream repo is perfectly accessible. The `+incompatible` suffix is a common Go version pattern for v2+ modules that haven't adopted Go modules semantics; this silently denies upstream context for a legitimate, common version format. Fix: strip `+incompatible` from the version before passing it as a ref, e.g., `version.replace(/\+incompatible$/, '')` before calling `refFor`.

findings.justification: Real [types-are-the-program] enumeration-gap bug: GO_MOD_REQUIRE_LINE also matches `replace`/`exclude` directives and captures the left-hand side of `=>`, yielding the wrong version for PRs that touch replace directives. Untested. The exact enumeration-gap class the laws prize.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** Edge-case / [LAW:types-are-the-program]: The `GO_MOD_REQUIRE_LINE` regex matches lines starting with `+` or `-` followed by a module path and version, but does not distinguish `require` from `replace` or `exclude` directives. For a go.mod `replace` directive like `+github.com/foo/bar v1.2.0 => github.com/foo/bar v1.3.0`, the regex captures `github.com/foo/bar` as the module path and `v1.2.0` (the left-hand side of `=>`) as the version — the actual bumped version is `v1.3.0` on the right side. This yields incorrect upstream context (fetched for the wrong version range) for PRs that modify replace directives. No test covers this distinction. Fix: either tighten the regex to match only inside a `require` block (e.g., by checking context lines for the `require (` header), or filter out lines containing `=>` before matching.

findings.justification: Real but very-low-impact: SAFE_MODULE_PATH excludes '_' from the domain class, so an underscored module domain fails the shape gate. The finding itself notes this is 'extremely rare'; safe, actionable widening.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** Edge-case: `SAFE_MODULE_PATH` uses `[a-zA-Z0-9.-]*` for the domain portion, which excludes the underscore character `_`. Go's module specification allows underscores in path elements including domain names (each element is made of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, and hyphens). While underscore-containing domain names for Go modules are extremely rare in practice, a legitimate module with an underscored domain (e.g., `my_domain.example/some/pkg`) would fail the shape check and never reach resolution, silently returning null. Since the regex is a security gate (not a Go spec parser), this is overly restrictive — underscores pose no URL-smuggling or scheme-injection risk. Fix: add `_` to the domain character class: `[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*`.

findings.justification: Real [behavior-not-structure] coverage gap tied to bug #3655283595: no test exercises the `+incompatible` suffix through refFor / fetchUpstreamChangeSummary. Valid test gap.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** [LAW:behavior-not-structure] Missing test coverage for the `+incompatible` version suffix in both `refFor` and `fetchUpstreamChangeSummary`. The `refFor` test at line 214 only exercises tagged versions (`v0.55.0`, `v3.27.3`) and pseudo-versions; the `fetchUpstreamChangeSummary` tests at line 224 use tagged versions only. The `+incompatible` suffix (e.g., `v2.0.0+incompatible`) is a real, common Go version pattern that would exercise the bug on line 167 of `src/dependency-diff.js`. A test passing `v2.0.0+incompatible` through `refFor` and verifying the stripped result, plus an end-to-end test in `fetchUpstreamChangeSummary` with an `+incompatible` version, would have caught the upstream compare failure.

findings.justification: Real edge case: the go.mod match only catches the root file, so nested-module bumps (tools/go.mod) are silently skipped in Go monorepos. Valid limitation, moderate impact.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** Edge case — `filteredFiles.find(f => f.filename === 'go.mod')` only matches the root `go.mod`. In Go monorepos with nested modules (e.g. `tools/go.mod`), version bumps in subdirectory `go.mod` files are silently skipped — the reviewer never sees upstream context for those dependency bumps. A `find` with exact equality also picks only the first match if multiple root-level `go.mod` files somehow exist in the diff. Use a broader match like `f.filename === 'go.mod' || f.filename.endsWith('/go.mod')` and collect bumps from every matching file.

findings.justification: Real bug: commits.slice(-MAX_COMMITS) takes the OLDEST 30 commits while the render text says 'most recent N' and files.slice(0, MAX_FILES) correctly takes the newest — the reviewer is shown the wrong end of the range. Clear off-by-direction defect.
findings.body: Bug: `commits.slice(-MAX_COMMITS)` takes the LAST (oldest) 30 commits from the GitHub compare API response, but the render text (line 232) says "most recent N shown" and the reviewer is instructed to check what changed upstream. GitHub's compare API returns commits in reverse chronological order (newest first), so `slice(-MAX_COMMITS)` yields the 30 oldest commits, while the comparable `files.slice(0, MAX_FILES)` on line 211 correctly takes the first (newest/changed) 50 files. The reviewer is shown the wrong end of the commit range. Fix: change to `commits.slice(0, MAX_COMMITS)` to get the most recent 30 commits, matching the render text and the files slice behavior.

findings.justification: Real [no-silent-failure] doc gap: README documents the 8-module cap but omits MAX_COMMITS/MAX_FILES truncation, so a user can't know upstream context is capped. Documentation-level.
findings.diffHunk:
@@ -173,6 +174,28 @@ jobs:
           DIFFICULTY_SCALING: "true"
 ```
 
+## Dependency diff context
+
+Set `DEPENDENCY_DIFF: "true"` to give the reviewer more than a version string when a PR bumps a `go.mod` requirement (for example, a Dependabot PR). When the diff changes a `go.mod` requirement line, the action resolves the bumped module to its GitHub repository and fetches the upstream commits and changed files between the old and new version via GitHub's compare API — then hands that as read-only context to the reviewer, which is instructed to check whether anything this repo actually calls into changed, broke, or was deprecated upstream, not just that a version moved.
+
+This runs entirely in the **host action** — the reviewing engine is never granted `Bash`, `WebFetch`, or any other network-capable tool; only the trusted Node process fetches the upstream diff, exactly as it already fetches the PR's own diff.
+
+Module resolution covers direct `github.com/...` module paths, the `golang.org/x/*` modules (mirrored 1:1 to `github.com/golang/*`), and falls back to the standard Go vanity-import discovery protocol for anything else. A module that can't be resolved to a GitHub repo (or whose compare call fails) is reported as such in the review context rather than silently omitted — the review still runs on the manifest diff alone. To bound both cost and prompt size, at most 8 bumped modules per PR get their upstream context fetched; any beyond that are named in the note as skipped, not silently dropped.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** [LAW:no-silent-failure] Documentation gap: the README documents the 8-module cap but omits the per-bump commit and file truncation caps (MAX_COMMITS=30, MAX_FILES=50 in src/dependency-diff.js:176-177). A user whose dependency bump spans 200 commits will see only the most recent 30 in the reviewer's context, potentially missing important changes (including breaking changes) from earlier in the range. The render template does flag truncation to the reviewer ("most recent N shown"), but the user reading these docs has no way to know this cap exists. The description should note both caps so users can decide whether to supplement with manual review.

findings.justification: Real security gap, confirmed and fixed in acd22cc: isPublicAddress covers RFC1918/loopback/link-local but omits RFC 6598 CGNAT space (100.64.0.0/10), which some cloud providers use for internal infrastructure — a bypass of the new SSRF guard. Present at the frozen head (the IPv4 range checks at line 93; isSafeHost landed in the frozen commit itself). Round-5 finding, re-anchored from :97@1641861.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** Security: `isPublicAddress` omits the RFC 6598 shared address space `100.64.0.0/10` (Carrier-Grade NAT). A diff-controlled module path whose hostname resolves to a CGNAT address — a range some cloud providers use for internal infrastructure — would pass the check and allow the discovery fetch to reach an internal service. The existing guards cover RFC 1918 and link-local correctly but miss this reserved range. Add `if (a === 100 && b >= 64 && b <= 127) return false;` after the `a === 10 || a === 127` check.

findings.justification: Real coverage gap, confirmed and fixed in acd22cc: no test asserts the truncation indicators ('most recent N shown' / 'first N shown') that renderDependencyDiffNote emits — at the frozen head the render fixture incidentally renders one but nothing pins the text, so a regression is invisible. Round-5 finding, re-anchored from :324@1641861 to the render test fixture.
findings.body: **Advisory (non-blocking):** Missing test: `renderDependencyDiffNote` truncation indicators are untested. The README documents that truncation is surfaced explicitly ("N total, most recent 30 shown" and "N total, first 50 shown"), and the implementation renders these at dependency-diff.js:240-241 when `totalCommits > commits.length` or `totalFiles > files.length`. The existing render test uses `totalCommits: 2` with 1 commit and `totalFiles: 1` with 1 file — matching counts, so truncation is never exercised. Add a test case with e.g. `totalCommits: 35, commits: (30 items)` to assert the rendered output includes `"most recent 30 shown"`. [LAW:behavior-not-structure]
